senses.definition: A remarkable person, object, or idea.

quotes.text: The funny part was, though, we were the worst skaters on the whole goddam^([sic]) rink. I mean the worst. And there were some lulus, too.
quotes.reference: 1951 July 16, J[erome] D[avid] Salinger, The Catcher in the Rye, Boston, Mass.: Little, Brown and Company, →OCLC, page 167:
1961, James Edward Grant, Clair Huffaker, The Comancheros, spoken by Jake Cutter (John Wayne):

quotes.text: Seriously, I mean it: From Russia, With Love is a real wowser, a lulu, a dilly and a smasheroo.
The job: a real lulu. The heiress to a cheese fortune has run off with a clarinet player in a swing band, and Hicks is dispatched to bring her home.
quotes.reference: 2025 October 9, Parul Sehgal, “Thomas Pynchon Saw Where America Was Headed. What Does He See Now?”, in The New York Times Magazine, New York, N.Y.: The New York Times Company, →ISSN, →OCLC:

senses.definition: A very attractive or alluring person.
A very bad mistake or error.
(slang) A fixed allowance paid to a legislator in lieu of reimbursement for actual expenses.
